Community-acquired pneumonia, right lower lobe (primary diagnosis)

Mr Halvorsen presented to the emergency department with a four-day history of productive cough, fever and increasing shortness of breath. On arrival his oxygen saturation was 89% on room air and his temperature was 38.9 °C.

A chest radiograph showed consolidation in the right lower zone without effusion.

He was treated with intravenous amoxicillin and oral clarithromycin, and was switched to oral antibiotics on day three once his fever had settled. His renal function improved with intravenous fluids and temporary withholding of ramipril and metformin. 1 He was mobilising independently and maintaining saturations above 94% on room air at the time of discharge.
1 Both medicines were restarted on 14 October 2026 after creatinine had returned to baseline.
